def-disk-like-capped-grope-height-one-an:
## Definition

Use the framed four-dimensional block and stage conventions for gropes in the cited definitions. A **capped grope** is a staged thickening whose bottom surface stage is joined along curves in a symplectic basis to higher surface stages, with the final tip circles capped by framed immersed disks. A **disk-like capped grope** has one connected bottom surface stage with exactly one attaching circle. Its **height** is the number of successive surface stages on each side of the symplectic basis, with caps terminating the stages. A disk-like capped grope has **height one and one-half**, written $1.5$, when its two sides have heights $(1,0)$ or $(0,1)$ in the asymmetric convention; equivalently, one half of the first-stage basis has one additional surface stage and the other half is capped immediately. The **attaching region** is the framed solid-torus neighborhood of the single attaching circle. For an immersed disk, a **double-point loop** is the image of a path in the domain disk joining the two preimages of a transverse self-intersection. In the disk-embedding property for an input capped grope, this loop is read as the corresponding element of the grope's fundamental group; choosing a basing path from the grope basepoint fixes that based element.
def-freedman-good-group-and-disk-embeddi:
## Definition

Let $X$ be a compact connected oriented topological $4$-manifold with nonempty boundary, let $x_0\in X$, and put $G=\pi_1(X,x_0)$. A **finite relative disk-embedding datum** consists of proper generic immersions $f_i:(D^2,S^1)\looparrowright(X,\partial X)$, $1\le i\le n$, whose boundary circles are embedded and pairwise disjoint, together with framed immersed spheres $g_i:S^2\looparrowright\operatorname{int}X$ that are algebraically dual to the disks. Here a generic immersion is locally a topological embedding except at finitely many double points, each with exactly two preimages whose image sheets are the coordinate planes $\mathbb R^2\times\{0\}$ and $\{0\}\times\mathbb R^2$ in a chart of $X$; proper means that the inverse image of $\partial X$ is exactly the domain boundary; and framed means that the normal microbundle has a chosen trivialization extending the specified boundary framing. Choose paths from $x_0$ to the immersed surfaces and orient the surfaces. Each transverse intersection $p$ of two surfaces contributes $\epsilon(p)g_p$ to $\lambda$, where $\epsilon(p)\in\{1,-1\}$ compares their induced local orientation with the chosen orientation of $X$, and $g_p\in G$ is the loop that travels along the chosen path to the first surface, then to $p$, and returns along the second surface and its chosen path. Thus $\lambda$ is a signed equivariant intersection sum in $\mathbb Z[G]$. Wall's self-intersection sum $\mu$ is the signed sum over self-double points in $\mathbb Z[G]/\langle g-g^{-1}:g\in G\rangle$, because interchanging the two sheets replaces a label by its inverse. The normal framing is a separate datum; its relative normal Euler or boundary-framing obstruction is zero precisely when the specified framing extends over the immersion. The spheres are **algebraically dual** when $\lambda(f_i,g_j)=\delta_{ij}$, $\lambda(g_i,g_j)=0$ for every $i,j$, and $\mu(g_i)=0$ for every $i$. The disk data are **algebraically unobstructed** when also $\lambda(f_i,f_j)=0$ for $i\ne j$ and $\mu(f_i)=0$ for every $i$.
def-good-fundamental-group-for-disk-embe:
## Definition

Let $\Gamma$ be a group. Say that $\Gamma$ is **good for the Freedman disk-embedding theorem** when it has the $\pi_1$-null disk property: for every disk-like capped grope $G^c$ of height $1.5$ with a chosen basepoint and every homomorphism $\phi:\pi_1(G^c)\to\Gamma$, there is an immersed disk whose framed boundary is the attaching region of $G^c$, such that each double-point loop of the disk, regarded after basing as an element of $\pi_1(G^c)$, is sent to the identity by $\phi$. This definition of a good group is a hypothesis on $\Gamma$; it does not assert that any particular group is good.
lem-freedman-casson-handle-skyscraper-an:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $X$ be an oriented topological $4$-manifold with boundary, and let $V\subset X$ be a connected relatively open neighborhood endowed with a specified smooth structure compatible with its smooth boundary collar and the given framed disk data, whose specified boundary collars and normal framings are smooth in this structure. Assume $\pi_1(V)$ is good for disk embedding. Let $f_i:(D^2,S^1)\looparrowright(V,V\cap\partial X)$ be a finite proper smooth generic disk datum with pairwise disjoint embedded framed boundaries, and framed smooth immersed spheres $g_i$ satisfying $\lambda(f_i,g_j)=\delta_{ij}$, $\lambda(g_i,g_j)=0$, $\mu(g_i)=0$, $\lambda(f_i,f_j)=0$ for $i\ne j$, and $\mu(f_i)=0$, computed in $\mathbb Z[\pi_1(V)]$.

There is a finite family of proper framed one-story capped-grope towers in $V$, of first-story height at least four, whose attaching regions are the Whitney circles for a regular homotopy of the $f_i$. Their bodies extend to embedded convergent skyscraper pinched neighborhoods, each with a relative standard-two-handle parameterization preserving its attaching solid torus and framing. The corresponding embedded framed Whitney disks give pairwise disjoint proper locally flat disks $\bar f_i$ homotopic to $f_i$ rel boundary and framing. They carry product normal neighborhoods supplied by this construction and framed immersed geometric duals $\bar g_i$ homotopic in $V$ to $g_i$.

In particular one may take $V=X$ when $X$ and the given maps, boundary collars and framings are smooth. No existence of a smoothing of a general topological neighborhood is asserted. The towers are capped-grope skyscrapers; an unrestricted Casson-handle construction is not assumed.
thm-freedman-disk-embedding-theorem-proo:
## Statement

Let $X$ be a compact oriented topological $4$-manifold with nonempty boundary. A **kinky handle** is a standard $2$-handle whose core disk has finitely many transverse self-plumbings; a **framed Casson-handle tower** is a nested sequence of such stages in which each self-plumbing point of one stage is replaced by a framed kinky handle at the next stage, with the attaching regions matching the preceding stage. Suppose a finite family of these tower $4$-neighborhoods is embedded pairwise disjointly in $X$, with attaching circles in $\partial X$, and carries the algebraic dual data of a disk-embedding datum. If each embedded tower has a homeomorphism of pairs to the standard open $2$-handle $D^2\times\mathbb R^2$ with attaching region $S^1\times\mathbb R^2$, then the inverse images of the cores $D^2\times\{0\}$ form a pairwise disjoint family of locally flat properly embedded disks in $X$, with the prescribed framed boundary circles.
thm-infinite-cyclic-group-is-good-for-di:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. The infinite cyclic group $\mathbb Z$ is good for the Freedman disk-embedding theorem, in the sense of the $\pi_1$-null disk property defined for a good fundamental group.
thm-freedman-disk-embedding-for-good-gro:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $X$ be a compact connected oriented smooth $4$-manifold with nonempty boundary and good fundamental group $G=\pi_1(X)$. Let $f_1,\ldots,f_n:(D^2,S^1)\looparrowright(X,\partial X)$ be proper generic immersed disks with pairwise disjoint embedded boundary circles. Suppose they admit framed immersed algebraically dual spheres $g_1,\ldots,g_n$ with $\lambda(f_i,g_j)=\delta_{ij}$, $\lambda(g_i,g_j)=0$, and $\mu(g_i)=0$, and suppose $\lambda(f_i,f_j)=0$ for $i\ne j$ and $\mu(f_i)=0$ for all $i$, in the equivariant intersection conventions of the disk-embedding data definition. Then the disks are homotopic rel boundary, preserving the boundary framings, to pairwise disjoint locally flat properly embedded disks in $X$.
lem-seifert-matrix-of-reverse-mirror-is-:
## Statement

Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot with a Seifert surface $F$ and ordered integral basis $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$, using $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$ for the positive-push Seifert matrix. Let $K^\dagger$ be the reverse mirror defined by the fixed orientation-reversing reflection followed by reversal of the knot orientation, and use the image basis on the reflected surface. The Seifert matrix of $K^\dagger$ in that basis is $-V$.
def-seifert-form-s-equivalence:
## Definition

Let $V$ be an integral Seifert matrix in the positive-push convention $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. Two integral Seifert forms are **S-equivalent** when they are related by a finite sequence of integral unimodular basis changes and algebraic tube additions or their inverses. A basis change replaces $V$ by $P^T V P$ for $P\in\operatorname{GL}_m(\mathbb Z)$. A tube addition replaces $V$ by
$$
\begin{pmatrix}
V&0&\rho\\
0&0&1\\
\rho^T&0&0
\end{pmatrix},\qquad \rho\in\mathbb Z^m,
$$
where the two new basis elements are the short and long curves of the added tube. The **empty Seifert form** is the unique bilinear form on the zero module, represented by the $0\times0$ matrix.
lem-alexander-one-seifert-form-is-s-equi:
## Statement

Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot with Alexander polynomial $\Delta_K(t)\doteq1$, where $\doteq$ denotes equality up to multiplication by a unit $\pm t^k$ of $\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$. For every Seifert surface $F$ of $K$ and every integral Seifert matrix $V$ of $F$ in the positive-push convention, the form represented by $V$ is S-equivalent over $\mathbb Z$ to the empty Seifert form.
lem-alexander-one-knot-has-trivial-alexa:
## Statement

Assume full AC. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot with $\Delta_K(t)\doteq1$, where $\doteq$ denotes equality up to multiplication by a unit $\pm t^k$ of $\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$. Then $K$ has a connected compact smooth oriented Seifert surface $F$ and an ordered geometric basis, represented by embedded simple closed curves $s_1,\ldots,s_g,\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_g$ for $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$, such that $s_i\cdot_Fs_j=0=\ell_i\cdot_F\ell_j$ and $s_i\cdot_F\ell_j=\delta_{ij}$, and the Seifert matrix in this basis has block form
$$V=\begin{pmatrix}0&I_g+U\\U^T&W\end{pmatrix},$$
where $U$ is strictly upper triangular and $W$ is symmetric with zero diagonal. Such a geometric symplectic basis and block matrix are called a trivial Alexander basis.
lem-alexander-one-knot-produces-a-good-g:
## Statement

Assume full AC. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot with $\Delta_K(t)\doteq1$. There is a connected compact smooth Seifert surface $F$ with a geometric symplectic basis $s_1,\ldots,s_g,\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_g$ whose positive-push matrix is
$$V=\begin{pmatrix}0&I_g+U\\ U^T&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad U\text{ strictly upper triangular}.$$
Place $F$ on the unit sphere in the literal radius-$3/2$ ball and join its boundary to the outer copy of $K$ by the radial product collar, rounding the inner junction away from that outer collar. Write $\Sigma$ for this proper surface. Its actual smooth normal thickening can be chosen so that the rounded complement
$$N=B^4_{3/2}\setminus\operatorname{int}\nu\Sigma$$
is compact, connected and smooth, with $\pi_1(N)\cong\mathbb Z$ generated by the positive normal meridian of $\Sigma$.

The fixed negative normal pushoffs of the short curves give disjoint framed circles $\delta_i\subset\partial N$. They bound proper framed smooth generic disks $\Delta_i$ in $N$ admitting framed smooth immersed spheres $f_i$ such that
$$\lambda(\Delta_i,f_j)=\delta_{ij},\quad \lambda(\Delta_i,\Delta_j)=0\ (i\ne j),\quad \mu(\Delta_i)=0,\quad \lambda(f_i,f_j)=0,\quad\mu(f_i)=0$$
in $\mathbb Z[\mathbb Z]$ with the specified Wall conventions. Along the fixed annuli from $\delta_i$ to $s_i\subset\Sigma$, their boundary framings agree with the normal directions of $s_i$ within $\Sigma$. Thus the data retain the actual ambient ball, complement, attaching circles and compression framings. The group is good when the infinite-cyclic good-group theorem is supplied. For $g=0$ the disk and sphere families are empty and the geometric complement assertion remains valid.
thm-alexander-polynomial-one-implies-top:
## Statement

Assume full AC. If a smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$ has Alexander polynomial $\Delta_K(t)\doteq1$, where $\doteq$ denotes equality up to multiplication by a unit $\pm t^k$ of $\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$, then there is a locally flat proper embedding $D^2\hookrightarrow B^4$ whose boundary is $K$. Here **topologically slice** means bounding such a locally flat proper disk; the conclusion asserts no smooth slice disk.
